t: LeetCode 2239 - Find Closest Number to Zero: Single-Pass Absolute Value Tracking
o: **Understanding the problem.** We must return the element of `nums` whose absolute value is smallest, i.e. the closest to zero, and if several elements tie we return the largest one. In example 1 the distances are 4, 2, 1, 4, 8, so `1` wins. In example 2 both `1` and `-1` sit at distance 1, and the tie-break rule selects `1`. With n up to 1000 even an O(n log n) sort fits easily, but folding the comparison into a single scan achieves O(n).
k: Distance to zero is simply the absolute value, so the comparison key is |x|.
On ties the larger value wins, and the positive twin is always the larger of the pair x, -x.
Comparing pairs (abs(x), x) lexicographically encodes both rules in one predicate.

a.n: Approach 1: Single Pass with Running Best
a.i: Keep the best candidate seen so far. A new element replaces it only when it is strictly closer to zero, or equally close but larger. This handles the tie-break automatically because among equal absolute values the positive number is the larger one.
s: Replace `best` if `abs(x) < abs(best)`, or if `abs(x) == abs(best)` and `x > best`.
a.t: O(n) - one comparison pass over the array.
a.sp: O(1) - only a scalar accumulator is kept.

a.i: Order the numbers by absolute value, breaking ties by descending value, and take the first element. Sorting states the tie-break rule declaratively at the cost of an extra logarithmic factor.
s: Sort with comparator: smaller `|x|` first; on equal `|x|`, larger `x` first.
a.t: O(n log n) - dominated by the sort.
a.sp: O(1) auxiliary in C++/JavaScript; O(n) for boxed arrays in Java/Python sorts.

w: Use the single-pass scan in an interview - it is optimal and shows you can fold a custom ordering into a linear reduction. Pitfalls: forgetting the tie-break (returning `-1` instead of `1` in example 2) and mishandling the single-element array. Natural follow-ups: closest element to an arbitrary target `t` (key becomes `|x - t|`) or the k closest numbers, where sorting or a heap becomes the tool of choice.
